h1: The 5 Best Google TV Projectors of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Google TV Projectors: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 5 projectors with built-in Google TV, scored on licensing, native resolution, brightness, voice control and noise.
summary: The WEMAX Google TV Smart Projector is the best pick here, built on official Google TV with a sealed optical engine and low fan noise. The 2000 ANSI Google TV-Licensed Projector is the one to buy if your room is not fully dark. The Smart 4K Projector adds a magnetic lens cover and a native 1080p panel. The WISHOLY Mini is the cheapest way into Google TV.
intro: Not every projector that says Google on the box runs the real thing. Plenty of budget models ship with a lookalike launcher, or with a Google assistant bolted onto a generic Android skin that cannot install Netflix. The phrase to hunt for is licensed or official, because it decides whether the apps you want will actually load and keep updating.

We ranked five projectors that advertise built-in Google TV, from a $50 to $100 mini to $200 to $500 models, by reviewing their listings for licensing language, native resolution, brightness, voice control and noise. Because the operating system is the point, we scored licensing claims above spec-sheet resolution, and we treated any 4K label that sits beside a 1080p panel with caution.

products.name: WEMAX Google TV Smart Projector
products.verdict: Official Google TV and Android with a fully sealed optical engine and low noise.
products.description:
The WEMAX is powered by official Google TV and Android, designed for an authentic home theater feel, with a fully sealed optical engine and low noise. A sealed engine keeps dust off the optics, and dust is what quietly dims and speckles a projector image after a year of use.

It takes first place because official licensing is the hardest thing to fake, and WEMAX states it plainly. It also costs $100 to $200, below the 2000 ANSI model, so you are not paying extra for the license.

Buy it for a bedroom or living room where fan whine would ruin quiet scenes. The listing does not give a lumen figure, so confirm brightness before you commit to a room with lamps on, and plan on dimmer lighting until you do.
pros: Sealed optical engine keeps dust out
cons: Needs a dimmed room until confirmed
products.idealFor: Quiet bedrooms and living rooms that want a properly licensed Google TV.
products.skipIf: You need a documented brightness number for a sunlit room.

products.name: 2000 ANSI Google TV-Licensed Projector
products.verdict: A 2000 ANSI lumen, Google TV-licensed projector with an AI voice remote.
products.description:
This projector is rated at 2000 ANSI lumens, is Google TV-licensed and ships with an AI voice remote for one-tap control. ANSI lumens come from a standardized measurement, so 2000 is a more honest figure than the inflated numbers on generic models, and it is enough to avoid fully darkening the room.

It ranks second because the WEMAX lists sealed optics and noise control that this one does not mention, though this one gives you the brightness number the WEMAX omits. Both state licensing, and this model sits in the $200 to $500 bracket for that extra light output.

Buy it if you watch with lamps on or have a window you cannot fully cover. Before ordering, open the full listing to check resolution, since the summary mentions no native panel and a bright image on a low-resolution panel still looks soft.
products.idealFor: Living rooms with lamps or partial window light.
products.skipIf: Your room goes fully dark and you want the quietest unit.

products.name: Smart 4K Projector with WiFi and Bluetooth
products.verdict: Google TV streaming, native 1080p with 4K input and a magnetic auto lens cover.
products.description:
This projector streams through Google TV with a voice assistant, features a native 1080p panel that accepts 4K signals and includes a magnetic auto lens cover. Stating native 1080p is the honest part: many cheaper projectors blur the line, and this listing tells you what the panel actually is.

It ranks third because the 2000 ANSI model gives a lumen figure and the WEMAX gives official licensing, while this one gives neither in its summary. The lens cover is a practical bonus that guards the glass against dust and fingerprints between sessions.

Buy it for a household with kids or a dusty room, where an exposed lens collects grime. Treat the 4K label as an input spec, because the panel is 1080p, and check the price bracket of $200 to $500 against what you actually get.
products.idealFor: Families and dusty rooms where the lens needs protection.
products.skipIf: You expect true 4K detail from the panel.

products.name: 4K Smart Projector with WiFi and Bluetooth
products.verdict: Powered by Google TV AI, with vast streaming content a mic button away.
products.description:
This model is powered by Google TV AI and promises instant access to vast streaming content, with a mic button on the remote for voice search. Voice search matters on a projector more than on a TV, because typing a title with a remote on a wall-sized screen is slow.

It ranks fourth because its summary says little about licensing, resolution or brightness, leaving the 4K name as the headline claim. Against the Smart 4K Projector above, it lacks a stated native panel, and against the WEMAX it lacks any sealed-engine note, yet it is priced at $200 to $500 alongside the stronger options.

Buy it if voice control is the feature you will use daily. Read the full listing for the native resolution and the brightness first, since the 4K name alone proves neither.
products.idealFor: Anyone who wants to find shows by voice rather than typing.
products.skipIf: You want licensing and lumen figures spelled out.

products.name: WISHOLY Mini Projector with WiFi and Bluetooth
products.verdict: A mini projector with built-in Google TV and a Google voice assistant at the lowest price.
products.description:
The WISHOLY is a mini projector with built-in Google TV and a Google voice assistant, plus WiFi and Bluetooth. At $50 to $100 it is the cheapest route to Google TV in this guide, and its compact size suits a bedroom shelf or a trip.

It ranks last because the title and bullet text lean on a 4K label with no native panel detail, and a price this low usually means a modest light engine. Next to the WEMAX, which costs $100 to $200 and states official licensing, the WISHOLY gives up verification, not features.

Buy it for casual watching in a dark room or while traveling. Confirm the licensing and the real resolution in the full listing before you rely on app support, because that is where very cheap Google TV projectors tend to cut corners.
products.idealFor: Casual dark-room viewing and travel on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You need guaranteed app licensing or a bright image.

whatMatters.detail: A licensed Google TV projector can install Netflix and other major apps and receive updates, while an unlicensed one may run a lookalike launcher that blocks them. The difference decides whether streaming works at all. Look for the words official or licensed in the listing, and be cautious of titles that only say Google voice assistant.

Native resolution is the pixel count of the panel itself. Many Google TV projectors accept a 4K signal but show it on a 1080p panel, as the Smart 4K Projector openly states. This matters for text and fine detail. Look for native 1080p or true 4K in the specification rather than trusting a headline label, and compare it with the screen size you plan to fill.

ANSI lumens measure brightness by a standard method, so 2000 means something concrete. Low figures need near darkness, while about 2000 tolerates lamps. A listing without any lumen number is hiding a weak point more often than not. Search the bullet points for ANSI and compare only like with like, because ISO, ANSI and plain lumens are not interchangeable.

Typing on a wall-sized screen is painful, so a mic-button remote makes browsing quick. Check that the remote has dedicated voice and streaming buttons and that the assistant is Google's own. A remote that pairs by Bluetooth also works without line of sight, which helps when the projector sits behind you or on a high shelf where you cannot aim a remote.

A noisy fan is the first thing you notice in a quiet scene, and dust on the optics is the thing that ruins images over time. A sealed optical engine, like the WEMAX lists, addresses both. Look for a stated decibel level or the word sealed, and keep vents clear of walls and fabric so the fan never has to strain.

faq.a: Licensed models should. The WEMAX states official Google TV and the 2000 ANSI model is Google TV-licensed, while the WISHOLY and 4K Smart Projector do not spell out licensing, so confirm app support in the full listing.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake buyers make with Google TV projectors?
faq.a: Trusting the 4K label. The Smart 4K Projector openly states a native 1080p panel with 4K input, and other models in this guide leave the panel unspecified. Check native resolution, not the headline.

faq.q: Is the 2000 ANSI model worth more than the WEMAX?
faq.a: If your room is not fully dark, yes. The 2000 ANSI Google TV-Licensed Projector lists 2000 ANSI lumens at $200 to $500, while the WEMAX at $100 to $200 gives no brightness figure.

faq.q: How do I set up Google TV on a projector?
faq.a: Plug in power, pair the remote, connect to WiFi and sign into your Google account. On the Smart 4K Projector and the WEMAX, use the voice button for search. Place the unit straight on to avoid keystone stretching.

faq.q: How do I protect the lens on these projectors?
faq.a: Keep it covered when idle. The Smart 4K Projector includes a magnetic auto lens cover, while the WEMAX has a sealed engine that keeps dust inside. For the WISHOLY, use a soft cloth and avoid touching the glass.

faq.q: Can I use Bluetooth headphones with the WISHOLY?
faq.a: Yes, the WISHOLY lists Bluetooth, so headphones or a speaker should pair through settings. If audio lags behind the picture, use a low-latency speaker, or run the sound through an HDMI soundbar.

finalTake: Buy the WEMAX Google TV Smart Projector for a quiet, properly licensed Google TV in a dim room. Step up to the 2000 ANSI Google TV-Licensed Projector when ambient light is a problem. Pick the Smart 4K Projector for the lens cover and the honest 1080p panel, and treat the WISHOLY as a budget trial. Verify licensing before you trust any of them with Netflix.
